topic: rebinding an old ledger: resewing the sections, guarding torn folds, gluing and pressing

provenance.author: CC (batch EN-2)
provenance.notes: napisane niezaleznie od korpusu PL, nie jest tlumaczeniem; urzadzenie obliczeniowe: higrometr warsztatowy

base: I am rebinding an old ledger whose sewing has failed and whose cloth cover is torn.
A spare board from another book lies on the bench and matches the thickness exactly.
A room hygrometer sits above the press, because the paper cockles badly in a damp week.
The text block has come apart into six sections with the thread rotted right through.
Should I resew the whole thing, or repair the sewing only where it has failed?
Resew the whole block, because a partial repair leaves old thread pulling against new.
Take the sections apart carefully and clean the folds before you thread a needle.
Old glue on the spine folds will stop the new sewing from lying properly flat.
Paste and time will soften that glue far better than any amount of patient scraping.
I softened the spine with paste and the old glue lifted off in long strips.
The folds are clean now, though two sections have torn along the first fold.
The room hygrometer showed sixty five percent while I worked, which felt rather damp.
The spare board has curled slightly on the bench since then, which cannot be good.
Should I guard those torn folds with paper, or simply sew through them as they are?
Guard them, since sewing through a torn fold tears the section further with every opening.
Cut narrow strips of thin Japanese paper and paste them along the inside of each fold.
Let them dry flat under a weight before you take the sections to the sewing frame.
Curling boards mean the room is too damp for pasting anything you intend to keep flat.
I guarded both torn sections and sewed the whole block on tapes as you suggested.
The spine swelled more than I expected and now sits noticeably thicker than the fore edge.
The block will not close properly and the sections splay apart near the top.
Have I used thread that is too heavy, or is the swelling normal at this stage?
Some swelling is normal, but that much suggests thread heavier than the paper needs.
Nip the spine in the press for an hour and much of it will disappear.
What remains gets shaped into the round when you back the block against the boards.
Use a finer thread next time and the swelling will look after itself entirely.
Nipping took out most of the swelling and rounding the spine dealt with the rest.
I glued the spine with a thin coat and lined it with linen afterwards.
The block now opens flat, though the glue feels rather hard along the whole spine.
Should I have used paste there instead, or is hard glue right for a heavy ledger?
Glue is right for a ledger, because paste alone will not hold a heavy block.
Hardness matters less once the linen lining takes most of the movement across the spine.
A thin coat is the important part, since thick glue makes the whole spine rigid.
Add a hollow tube over the lining and the covering will move without cracking.
The hollow tube made an enormous difference and the ledger opens easily to any page.
I covered it in book cloth and the corners came out neat on the second attempt.
One board shows a faint ridge where the turn in overlaps beneath the pastedown.
Is that worth pulling apart and redoing, or will the ridge settle under steady pressure?
It will settle, provided you press the book properly between boards for several days.
Ridges from a turn in flatten out once the covering dries under steady even weight.
Pull the whole cover apart only if the ridge sits where a hand rests constantly.
Otherwise leave it, because every rebinding carries a few marks of its own making.
